pull.title: KAFKA-21306: Drop tasks already on the new process when a static streams member rejoins
pull.body:
In a streams group, one process must never hold the same task twice, for
example as an active task on one member and as a standby task on
another. The reconciler checks this only when it grants a task to a
member. A task that the member already holds and still has in its target
assignment is kept without the check.

A static member that rejoins under a new member ID gets a copy of its
previous member, including the previous member's assigned tasks. If the
member rejoins from a different process, the copied tasks move to the
new process with it, and none of them is checked. When another member on
the new process already holds one of those tasks, that process now holds
the task twice. A Kafka Streams client gets here when an instance
restarts under a new process ID, for example because its topology has no
persistent stores: if one stream thread rejoins and is given the standby
of a task before the thread that ran the task as active rejoins, both
threads are told to run the task.

With this change, when a static member rejoins from a different process,
the new member keeps only the copied tasks that no member holds on the
new process, in any role. The dropped tasks stay in the target
assignment, so the reconciler grants them again later with its usual
checks. Until then, a dropped task has no owner on the new process
instead of two. When the process is unchanged, or no copied task is held
on the new process, the member keeps all its tasks as before.

`testStaticMemberRejoinFromNewProcessDropsTaskHeldThereAsStandby` drives
the restart above with the sticky assignor and one standby replica. The
second thread rejoins first and gets the standby. The first thread then
rejoins and gets no active task, and the new process holds the task only
as a standby.

Reviewers: Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>, Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

reviews.body:
Agree with the analysis. It’s a corner case and it heals itself, but we should still fix it since one process briefly gets told to run the same task twice. One small correction from trying it out: once the second rebalance runs, the sticky assignor promotes M2’s standby to active, and M1 ends up empty. So it recovers, but not by M1 getting the active task back.

I’m not keen on remapping all members of p-old to p-new. Besides the case where a client comes back with more members, we’d be guessing about members that aren’t heartbeating. Nothing guarantees the instance IDs from p-old all come back on the same new process.

I’d go for something simpler than the current fix. When a static member rejoins from a different process, don’t copy its current assignment at all, and only keep the relabeled target assignment. The reconciler then grants the tasks with its usual checks, so we don’t need a second copy of the one-process check in the static join path. We also don’t lose anything, because the new process has no local state for those tasks anyway. Conflicting tasks wait for the next rebalance exactly as they do with the current PR.

I agree the root cause is the new process ID. That only happens for apps without persistent stores, because with persistent stores the process ID is kept in the state directory. Fixing it would mean the client keeps its process ID across restarts, which I’d treat as a separate change.

review_comments.body: Since this is a corner case, could we simplify this: when a static member rejoins from a different process, don't copy its assigned tasks at all and only keep the relabeled target assignment, so the reconciler grants them with its usual checks? The new process has no local state for those tasks anyway, so we don't lose much, and we wouldn't need a second copy of the one-process check here. The same could then apply to the other join paths (e.g. rejoining with the same member ID after leaving with -2), though I don't think Streams can hit those today.

Could we continue the test until the task is running again? E.g. sleep past the assignment interval and heartbeat both members. When I tried that, the sticky assignor promotes the second member's standby to active and the first member ends up empty. Right now the test would also pass if the task stayed unassigned forever.

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for the PR. -- I am not sure if the proposed fix is the right one or not. Maybe @lucasbru @squah-confluent can chime in?

My understanding is, that we currently present stale group metadata to the assignor, and thus, the assignor might incorrectly assign a standby to a member in the group, even if a "sibling member" (ie, member of a different thread within the same Kafka Streams clients) hold a corresponding active task. Example:

Single instance in the group with two static members M1 and M2. M1 hold active tasks t-active. t-standby cannot be assigned, because we have only one instance in the group. We do a rolling bounce (with -2 temp leave), and M2 re-join first with a new processId. This triggers an assignor run, and we pass in M1 with the old member m1-old and old processId p-old, while we did re-map M2 onto an new memberId m2-new and use the new processId p-new. The assignor now incorrectly thinks there is two clients, and incorrectly assigns t-standby to M2. Later, when M1 re-joins, before this fix we incorrectly give t-active to M1, and with this fix, we hold off to give t-active to M1. When M1 re-joins, it also triggers a rebalance (which might be delayed base on assignment-interval config), and when the second rebalance runs, it now correctly sees both member using processId p-new, and would only assign t-active and omit t-standby again. So the problem is self-healing.

However, I am wondering if it would be better to try to re-map all member of the same processId p-old, to p-new, whenever a member re-joins? There is one corner case though: it's possible that a client restarts with more members: for this case building on our example from above, if we re-start with 3 members and the new/third member joins first, it's not possible to link it to the old processId...

So maybe the current fix is the best we can do anyway? -- Or course, the root cause of the issue is, that we trigger a rebalance on a new processId to begin with, and if we could fix this issue, it would be much better.

Thoughts?

KAFKA-21306: Drop tasks already on the new process when a static streams member rejoins

for example as an active task on one member and as a standby task on

process now holds the task twice. A Kafka Streams client gets here
when an instance restarts under a new process ID, for example because
its topology has no persistent stores: if one stream thread rejoins
